quests.instruction: Before takeoff, which task is part of a pilot's preparation?
options: Loading the passengers' luggage
Checking fuel and instruments
Guiding planes by radio from the tower
quests.hint: Think about making sure the plane itself is ready.
quests.explanation: Pilots check fuel, instruments, and the flight plan before takeoff. Baggage handlers load luggage, and controllers guide planes from the tower.
quests.funFact: A flight plan lists the route, the fuel needed, and other airports where the plane could land if necessary.

quests.instruction: A baker is making bread. Which step happens before the loaves are shaped?
options: Slicing the cooled loaves for the shop
Wrapping the finished bread in paper
Mixing and kneading the dough
quests.hint: Think about what has to exist before it can be shaped.
quests.explanation: Bakers mix and knead dough first, let it rise, shape it, bake it, and finally cool, slice, or wrap it.
quests.funFact: Kneading makes dough stretchy, which helps bread rise and gives it a soft inside.

quests.instruction: At the end of a shift, a nurse writes notes about each patient. Why?
options: So the next team knows what happened
So patients can read them for fun later
So the ward looks neater and a lot tidier
quests.correctAnswer: So the next team knows what happened
quests.hint: Think about another nurse arriving as the shift changes.
quests.explanation: Written notes help care teams share important information when one shift ends and another begins.
quests.funFact: Hospitals work day and night, so nurses work in shifts to care for patients around the clock.

quests.instruction: After the restaurant closes, which task helps keep the kitchen safe for the next day?
options: Leaving hot pots on the stove all night
Switching off all of the smoke alarms
Cleaning surfaces and storing food
quests.hint: Think about leaving the kitchen ready for tomorrow.
quests.explanation: Cleaning and storing food properly keeps kitchens safe and stops food from spoiling.
quests.funFact: Many kitchens label stored food with the date so cooks know how fresh it is.

quests.instruction: Besides checking out books, which task might a librarian do?
options: Reading stories aloud to children
Repairing car engines for customers
Checking patients' blood pressure
quests.hint: Think about events libraries hold for young readers.
quests.explanation: Many librarians run story times, help with research, and organize new books, as well as checking items out.
quests.funFact: Some libraries also lend other things, such as board games or telescopes.

quests.instruction: Before the pool opens for the day, which task does a lifeguard do?
options: Planning the swimmers' lunch menu
Checking the water and rescue gear
Counting the ticket money
quests.correctAnswer: Checking the water and rescue gear
quests.hint: Think about being ready before anyone jumps in.
quests.explanation: Lifeguards check the water, the pool area, and the rescue equipment before opening, so they are ready to prevent problems.
quests.funFact: Many pools post depth markers and rules so swimmers know where it is safe to swim.

quests.instruction: On a school trip, which of these is a teacher's responsibility?
options: Keeping track of every single child
Driving the school bus there
Selling snacks to other visitors
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping track of every single child
quests.hint: Think about counting heads at every stop.
quests.explanation: On trips, teachers count children, give clear instructions, and make sure everyone stays safe.
quests.funFact: Many teachers use a buddy system, so each child has a partner to stay with.

quests.instruction: A pharmacist double-checks the name and dose on every medicine label. Why?
options: So the label looks neat and tidy
So each person gets the right medicine
So the bag uses less paper
quests.correctAnswer: So each person gets the right medicine
quests.hint: Think about two people with very similar names.
quests.explanation: Mistakes with medicine can be harmful, so pharmacists check labels carefully.
quests.funFact: Pharmacists also answer questions about how medicines should be stored.

quests.instruction: A zookeeper notices that one animal has stopped eating its food. What should the zookeeper do?
options: Wait a week and see what happens
Offer a different animal's food
Tell the zoo's veterinary team
quests.hint: Think about who can check whether the animal is unwell.
quests.explanation: Zookeepers watch animals closely, and a change in eating is a sign they should tell the veterinary team.
quests.funFact: Zoo teams keep daily records of what each animal eats and how it behaves.

quests.instruction: Water is spraying from a loose pipe in a school bathroom. What should a plumber do first?
options: Paint the pipe
Turn off the water supply
Turn up the pressure
quests.hint: Think about stopping the leak from getting worse.
quests.explanation: Turning off the water stops more from escaping and makes the repair safer and tidier.
quests.funFact: Most homes have a main shut-off valve that stops water to the whole house.

quests.instruction: A customer tells a café worker they cannot have dairy. What is the barista's most responsible choice?
options: Make the usual drink to save time
Guess which milk is probably safe
Check the ingredients carefully
quests.hint: Think about keeping the customer healthy.
quests.explanation: Workers who serve food must take allergies seriously, check ingredients, and use clean equipment.
quests.funFact: Many cafes list their ingredients or keep allergy information so customers can choose safely.

quests.instruction: During a fitting, a tailor pins the cloth and makes chalk marks. Why?
options: So changes go in the right places
So the cloth changes color overnight
So the jacket becomes heavier to wear
quests.correctAnswer: So changes go in the right places
quests.hint: Think about what will guide the needle later.
quests.explanation: Pins and chalk marks show exactly where to adjust the cloth, so the final sewing fits the person.
quests.funFact: Tailors often fit clothes while the customer stands still, so they can see how the cloth hangs.

quests.instruction: A person has fainted, and paramedics arrive to help. What do they check first?
options: Whether the person is breathing
The size of the person's shoes
What the person ate last week
quests.hint: Think about the most important body signs.
quests.explanation: Paramedics start by checking responsiveness and breathing, because these show how urgently help is needed.
quests.funFact: Paramedics are trained to stay calm and speak clearly so patients feel reassured.

quests.instruction: At a school visit, a firefighter explains that smoke rises. What should children do to stay safer if a room fills with smoke?
options: Stand tall so you can see better
Hide in a closet until it clears
Stay low and head for the exit
quests.correctAnswer: Stay low and head for the exit
quests.hint: Think about where the cleanest air is in a smoky room.
quests.explanation: Smoke rises, so the air is clearer near the floor. Staying low and moving to the exit is the safest plan.
quests.funFact: Many fire stations welcome school visits so children can see the gear and ask questions.

quests.instruction: A pet owner is worried because a rabbit has stopped eating. What does the vet do first?
options: Give the rabbit a bath right away
Ask questions and examine the rabbit
Send the owner home without a check
quests.correctAnswer: Ask questions and examine the rabbit
quests.hint: Think about finding out what is wrong before choosing a treatment.
quests.explanation: Vets ask owners questions and examine the animal to find out what is wrong before treating it.
quests.funFact: Pets often hide when they feel unwell, so an owner's observations help vets a lot.

quests.instruction: A shopper notices they were charged twice for one item. What should the cashier do?
options: Say nothing and hope it is fine
Fix the mistake and apologize
Charge the customer a third time
quests.hint: Think about being fair and honest.
quests.explanation: Cashiers check receipts and correct errors, so customers pay the right amount.
quests.funFact: Many stores have a customer service desk for returns and questions.

quests.instruction: A passenger says they are late for a train. What is the most helpful and responsible thing a taxi driver can do?
options: Choose the quickest safe route
Drive faster than the speed limit
Stop for a long snack on the way there
quests.hint: Think about helping the passenger without breaking the rules.
quests.explanation: Taxi drivers can help by choosing a good route, but they must always follow traffic rules to keep everyone safe.
quests.funFact: Many taxi drivers use maps or traffic apps to find the quickest route.

quests.instruction: A customer feels nervous about a big change of hairstyle. What is the best way for the hairdresser to respond?
options: Cut very quickly without saying a word
Choose a brand-new style without asking
Explain and check they feel comfortable
quests.correctAnswer: Explain and check they feel comfortable
quests.hint: Think about listening and explaining.
quests.explanation: Good service means listening, explaining what will happen, and checking that the customer feels comfortable.
quests.funFact: Hairdressers often look at photos with customers to be sure they understand the style they want.

quests.instruction: Who opens and locks the school building each day and looks after its heating and small repairs?
options: Crossing Guard
School Counselor
School Caretaker
quests.hint: Think about who looks after the building itself.
quests.explanation: School caretakers keep buildings safe, working, and ready for use, from unlocking doors to fixing small problems.
quests.funFact: Caretakers often arrive before everyone else and leave after everyone has gone.

quests.instruction: Which worker keeps the glass on tall office buildings clear and clean?
options: Window Cleaner
Glazier
House Painter
quests.hint: Think about someone who makes glass sparkle, not someone who replaces it.
quests.explanation: Window cleaners wash glass so people can see through it. Glaziers repair or replace the glass itself.
quests.funFact: Window cleaners use a squeegee, a rubber blade that pulls water off the glass.

quests.instruction: Why do railway workers regularly inspect the tracks?
options: To make the rails shiny and new
To find small problems early
To count the passengers on board
quests.hint: Think about trains that cannot swerve around a problem.
quests.explanation: Inspections find damage or loose parts early, so trains can travel safely.
quests.funFact: Railway workers follow strict safety rules whenever they work near the tracks.

quests.instruction: Who plans the schedule, books the place, and organizes all the details for a big wedding or conference?
options: Photographer
Sound Engineer
Event Planner
quests.hint: Think about someone who coordinates many small details so everything runs smoothly.
quests.explanation: Event planners organize schedules, venues, and suppliers so that everything happens on time.
quests.funFact: Event planners often make checklists that list every task and its deadline.

quests.instruction: A builder reads the building plan carefully before starting work. Why?
options: To know what to build and where
To pick a color for the walls
To find out when lunch is
quests.correctAnswer: To know what to build and where
quests.hint: Think about instructions for the whole building.
quests.explanation: Building plans show sizes, positions, and materials, so workers can build correctly and safely.
quests.funFact: Blueprints got their name from an old printing method that made white lines on blue paper.

quests.instruction: Before photographing a school play, which task helps a photographer prepare?
options: Paint the stage so it looks fresh
Visit the hall to check lighting and angles
Teach the actors their lines
quests.correctAnswer: Visit the hall to check lighting and angles
quests.hint: Think about knowing the space before the show begins.
quests.explanation: Checking the light and possible positions helps photographers plan where to stand and which camera settings to use.
quests.funFact: Photographers often arrive early at events so they can test their equipment.

quests.instruction: Rain is forecast for tomorrow, so a farmer harvests wheat today. Which responsibility does this show?
options: Taking customers' orders at a counter
Filling in forms at a busy front desk
Planning work around the weather
quests.hint: Think about why timing matters for crops.
quests.explanation: Farmers watch weather forecasts, because rain, wind, and sun affect when crops should be harvested.
quests.funFact: Farmers often work long days at busy times of the year, such as harvest.

quests.instruction: Maya's coach notices that a player is limping. What is the most responsible choice?
options: Let her rest and ask for help
Tell her to run faster to warm up
Ignore it until the whole game ends
quests.correctAnswer: Let her rest and ask for help
quests.hint: Think about protecting the player's health.
quests.explanation: Coaches care about players' safety, so they stop the activity and get help if someone may be hurt.
quests.funFact: Many sports teams keep a first-aid kit at every practice.

quests.instruction: Before a concert, a musician tunes their instrument. Why?
options: So it looks shinier on the stage
So the notes sound right together
So it weighs a little less to carry
quests.correctAnswer: So the notes sound right together
quests.hint: Think about playing with others in a band.
quests.explanation: Tuning adjusts an instrument so its notes match, which helps a group sound pleasant together.
quests.funFact: Orchestras often tune to a single note from one instrument so everyone starts together.

quests.instruction: A nurse, a lifeguard, and a teacher all work in different places. Which responsibility do they share?
options: Keeping people safe and cared for
Selling tickets to lots of customers
Repairing machines in a workshop
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping people safe and cared for
quests.hint: Think about the people each of them looks after every day.
quests.explanation: Nurses care for patients, lifeguards watch swimmers, and teachers look after students, so each one helps keep people safe.
quests.funFact: Many jobs involve caring for others, even outside hospitals and schools.

quests.instruction: A school bus driver walks around the bus before the morning trip. Which task is most important?
options: Washing the windows until shiny
Counting the seats and the rows
Checking tires, lights, and mirrors
quests.hint: Think about everything that must work for a safe trip.
quests.explanation: Drivers check tires, lights, brakes, and mirrors before a trip, because a small fault can become a big problem on the road.
quests.funFact: Drivers often check the bus again at the end of the day and report any faults.

quests.instruction: Which statement best describes a responsible worker?
options: Always finishes first, whatever happens
Works carefully, even when alone
Only does the tasks that seem fun
quests.hint: Think about being trusted by others.
quests.explanation: Being careful and honest in daily tasks is one of the most important parts of any job.
quests.funFact: Many workers tick off tasks when they finish them, so teams know what is done.
